summary: N. Aiyaswami Sastri worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a professor at Sri Venkateswara Oriental College (attested 1940) and later as a professor at Visva-Bharati University (attested 1971).
N. D. Mironov was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Leipzig University (~1902–1903) and studied under Hermann Jacobi (~1903–1905) and Heinrich Hübschmann.
N. J. Karthika works in computational Indology. She completed her Ph.D. at the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay and also held an academic post there.

N. Veezhinathan is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who earned a PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University in 1964. He studied under A. Sankaran, T. S. Srinivasa Sastri, and T. M. P. Mahadevan, and was appointed Lecturer at Madras in 1964.

N. Venkataramanayya was a scholar of Indology and history and archaeology who studied under Ferrand E. Corley. He served as Reader at the University of Madras and as Deputy Director for Epigraphy at Andhra Pradesh's Department of Archaeology and Museums.

Nae Ionescu was a philosopher who studied at the University of Bucharest (~1908–1912), Göttingen (~1913–1914), and Munich (~1916–1919). He held a post at the University of Bucharest (~1920–1938), where he taught Mircea Eliade.
Nagin J. Shah is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He succeeded Dalsukh Malvania as Acting Director at the L.D. Institute of Indology (attested 1968) and taught Maria Heim.

Nalinaksha Dutt was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Calcutta, Chittagong College, Presidency College, and SOAS/London (DLitt 1930) under Louis de La Vallée Poussin. He headed Calcutta's Pali Department (~1930–1958) and presided over the Asiatic Society (1959–1961).

Nalini Balbir is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Colette Caillat. She held posts at CNRS (1982–1988), Sorbonne Nouvelle University (Professor from 1988), and École Pratique des Hautes Études (Directeur d'Études from 2000).
Nalini Devdas is a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. She completed her Ph.D. at Concordia University under Leslie C. Orr and held an academic post at Carleton University.

Nam-lin Hur specializes in Japanology, religious studies, and history. Educated at the University of Tokyo and under Helen Hardacre, he was a postdoctoral fellow at Harvard and became professor of Japanese history and religious culture at British Columbia (attested 2000).

Naman P. Ahuja is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who completed his doctorate at SOAS University of London. He became Professor of Indian Art and Architecture at Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 2018).

Namgyal Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies teacher who studied at Toronto Baptist Seminary, Michigan, and under Sayadaw U Thila Wunta, Mahasi Sayadaw, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje. He founded Kagyu Samye Ling (1965) and the Dharma Centre of Canada (1966).

Namio Egami was a historian and archaeologist of Central Asian and Iranian studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (1927–1930), taught there (~1935–1967), and later served as Director of the Ancient Orient Museum (~1978–2002).
Namita Das is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. She completed her Ph.D. at Gauhati University under the doctoral supervision of Sibnath Sarma.

Namkhai Norbu was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Derge Gonchen and under several traditional masters, and served as Professor at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (1962–1992) and University of Naples Federico II (~1964–1992).

Nancy E. Levine is a scholar of Tibetology and anthropology. She has held posts at the University of California, Los Angeles, as Associate Professor of anthropology (attested 1998) and Professor of Anthropology (attested 2026).

Nancy G. Lin is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. She completed graduate work at Columbia and earned a Ph.D. from UC Berkeley, later serving as professor at the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (attested 2026).

Nancy Hock is a specialist in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her Ph.D. at the University of California, Berkeley (1987) under Joanna Gottfried Williams and held a post at the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco (attested 1987).

Nancy McCagney is a scholar in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. She studied under Chögyam Trungpa, Ninian Smart, Gerald James Larson, William F. Powell, and Andrew Rawlinson, and held a post at the University of Delaware (attested 1997).
